title: P0 · Before the season — keys and codes are shared
description: Malaysia's HIE publishes the public keys it signs health documents with to the WHO GDHCN trust network, and shares the national code systems its IPS uses with the WHO Terminology Service. Nothing about Kamal yet: this is what lets a Saudi clinic trust and read a Malaysian record months later. Step A of the overview of key process flows.

steps.title: Keys and codes are shared
steps.headline: Before anyone travels, Malaysia's signing keys and code systems reach the trust network, so a Saudi clinic can trust and read a Malaysian record months later.
steps.narrative: Malaysia's HIE publishes the public keys it signs health documents with to the WHO GDHCN trust network, and shares the national code systems its IPS uses with the WHO Terminology Service. Nothing about Kamal yet: this is what lets a Saudi clinic trust and read a Malaysian record months later. Step A of the overview of key process flows.

experiences.doing: Publishes the public keys it signs health documents with to GDHCN, and shares its national code systems with the WHO Terminology Service.
Lists Malaysia's keys alongside those of every other participant, including KSA.

steps.painPoint: Without published keys, a Saudi clinic has no way to tell a genuine Malaysian record from a forged one.
steps.enabler: Both countries take part in one trust network, so each trusts the other's keys without a bilateral agreement.
steps.policy: Which Malaysian institution signs health documents on behalf of the health sector, and who in KSA decides to accept that signature?

handoff.summary: Malaysia's keys and code systems are known to the trust network
handoff.payload: Public signing keys (DSCs); national code systems

gaps: No business process or transaction for publishing keys or terminologies.
